newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta Central Bank Governor says no recession.
newsitem.headline: Malta Central Bank Governor says no recession.

text.p: Malta Central Bank governor Francis Vassallo said on Thursday Malta was experiencing an economic slowdown but was not in recession.
Speaking as new Finance Minister Leo Brincat made his first visit to the Central Bank, Vassallo said Malta's economy had in the past few months experienced a slowdown.
"There is an economic slowdown but not a recession and if we continue arguing there is a recession we will bring one about," he said.
"The economic slowdown is due to uncertainty surrounding the change in the taxation system but once this is ironed out there is no reason for the economy not to continue growing.

"The economy will not continue to grow at the same rate as before. The growth rate should be slower, enabling the country to sustain economic performance. We will experience sustainable growth which will not overheat the economy," Vassallo said.

The Labour government, elected last October, is holding talks on a system to replace value added tax with a system that will include customs and excise duties and a tax on products and services. It is due to be introduced by the end of summer.
